versions.changelog: Requires json >= 3.0.1; HttpResponse.json() still returns a JsonValue; new HttpResponse.json_doc() returns a read-only JsonDoc.
Security: requires tls >= 1.4.3 (earlier tls accepted certificates issued by non-CA certificates, letting any trusted certificate impersonate any server).
Requires tls >= 1.4.4 (security hardening: truncation protection, RSA PKCS#1 out-of-bounds read fix, X25519 low-order rejection, TLS 1.3 downgrade sentinel).
No getenv/clock_gettime declarations of its own, so programs using HttpClient with std.os.getenv, open() or the std time functions compile; random multipart boundaries; requires tls 1.7.0.
tcp 2.0.0: TlsSocket(sock.detach()); plain-HTTP sends complete or raise; no SIGPIPE.

No linker flags: zlib/libzstd/libbrotlidec are opened at runtime and Accept-Encoding lists only what can be decoded (builds with $(cat .mojo_flags) alone). Fixed HTTP/2 PADDED frames (google.com gzip failed).
Requires Mojo >= 1.2.0 (builds on 1.2, deprecation warnings cleared). No API or behavior change. Needs json >= 3.1.0.

Adds total_timeout_secs deadline, retries (max_retries), HTTP/2 multiplexing (get_many), and configurable max_response_bytes/max_header_bytes/max_batch_bytes. Additive API. Behavior changes: POST/PATCH no longer replayed on a stale pooled connection unless retry_non_idempotent; h1 headers >1 MB and h2 bodies >100 MB rejected; ENABLE_PUSH=0 sent.

Bug fixes, no API change. Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding are matched as header names only (a header such as X-Amz-Meta-Content-Length, or a value containing the text, no longer truncates the body and desyncs the keep-alive connection). Chunked bodies are detected when Transfer-Encoding is the last header (S3 listings: ~6.5 s to ~0.7 s).

HTTP/1.1 response framing is decided once, from the parsed headers. Behavior change: ambiguous framing now raises ParseError (differing or non-numeric Content-Length, whitespace before the colon or a line continuation in Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding, unsupported transfer codings such as 'gzip, chunked', chunked not last). Transfer-Encoding wins over Content-Length, and such connections are not reused. Chunked trailers split across reads no longer time out. max_response_bytes above 100 MB now works for HTTP/1.1. No API changes; pin to 1.7.1 if you rely on lenient parsing.

Bug fixes, no API change. Security: a chunk size such as 7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF no longer aborts the process (ChunkedBodyError), and a malformed HPACK string from an HTTP/2 server raises instead of reading past the block. Performance: chunked bodies are decoded in linear time (4x16 MiB: 6.4 s to 0.2 s), large bodies are copied faster (#47) and no longer held twice in memory (1.8.0 regression). Brotli bodies that expand more than 8x now decode (#45).

Additive. HttpClient gains trust_env (False ignores HTTP(S)_PROXY/NO_PROXY), decompress (False returns bodies as sent), default_content_type ("" sends none) and a connections_opened counter. Interim 1xx responses are skipped and 204/304 no longer wait for a body on keep-alive connections. Caller-supplied Host, User-Agent and Connection headers replace the defaults. Behavior change: empty POST/PUT/PATCH now send Content-Length: 0, and get_stream caps the response header block at max_header_bytes. Thanks to winding-lines for #40, #41, #42 and #46.

Security hardening; rejects traffic that worked before (pin 1.9.0 if you rely on it). Cookies: Domain must cover the request host, control characters rejected, jar capped (3000 cookies, 4096 bytes each). Redirects drop Authorization, Cookie and Proxy-Authorization when the scheme, host or port changes. A chunked body cut before its terminal chunk raises ChunkedBodyError, and get_stream raises on a body shorter than Content-Length. Decompressed output is capped by max_response_bytes. NUL/control characters are rejected in header names, values and paths. HPACK table size updates above the advertised limit are errors. allow_private_ips still does not apply to the target of a proxied request.

A TLS connection whose server answers no ALPN protocol now uses HTTP/1.1 on that same connection: the HTTP/2 preface probe and the second handshake are gone (a GET to a TLS 1.2 server used to open 2 connections). Requires tls >= 1.11.0, which reports the ALPN result on TLS 1.2, so a TLS 1.2 server that selects h2 still gets h2. Behavior change: servers that speak h2 without ALPN are no longer reached (RFC 9113 3.2). Thanks to winding-lines for #48.

A chunked response body over 100 MB failed whatever max_response_bytes was set to; the chunk decoder now uses the client's limit. A single chunk over 256 MB is still rejected. Thanks to winding-lines for the report (#28).

Binary request bodies: post/put/patch/delete take List[UInt8] or Span[UInt8]; a public request(method, url, [body], [headers]) for any method; HttpResponse.content() (zero-copy view) and to_bytes() (owned copy). Additive; existing signatures unchanged. Thanks to winding-lines (#37).

request_many(List[Request]) sends several requests at once, each with its own method, headers and body (a Range read per request). GET, HEAD and OPTIONS to one HTTP/2 host share a connection and run concurrently; everything else goes one by one. Session.request_many merges session headers. Additive; get_many is now a wrapper. Refs #35.
